label: early original-phase input (t=1-5) of a k/u/d/v/q/h-type token after a 1/v/m/u-type token
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase, at early positions t=1..5. It peaks at t=2-3 and is never active at t=0. It is essentially silent at the delimiter and throughout the copy phase. Within that window it depends on the current token: k, u, d, v, q and h fire most (k at 22%, about 4x the base rate), then e, w, 1 and y. It also depends on the preceding context: rates are higher when earlier inputs include 1, v, m or u, and it fires more on the first occurrence of a token. The strongest activations are k or u at t=2-3 after a prefix such as v 1 / 1 1 / m v 1. The position window alone covers 93% of activation mass but has precision 0.15. The chosen predicate (early position, current token in K, some earlier input in A) reaches dev F1 0.61 and mass recall 0.81. It looks like a graded function of a token-identity mix over the first few inputs, so no single crisp boolean captures it fully.
